summary: The extension theorem and both applications are proved without mathematical errors or gaps. The Boolean downset input applies with the stated finite-ground-set map, including the empty label. The shifted core copies lie in the original support, are disjoint at each fixed threshold, and preserve their exact original masses. The halfspace argument handles zero restricted normals and boundary atoms; selecting one threshold per label prevents double counting of sampled roots. The ordered-energy estimate and Holder comparison yield the stated constant with four factors of the full mixed normalizer. Only cutoffs in the declared finite set are used. Both four-site predecessor laws, ambient depths, normalizers, hypotheses, and coefficients match under the explicit maps, and the convex epigraph interpretation follows from the stated slope inequalities. The cases s=0, T=0, beta=0, tied energies, heterogeneous three-site costs, and lower affine ranks are covered.
